variants.label: Jack's template (14 Nov); greeting line made a slot; no opt-out line in the original, it is added when sending
variants.text:
Hi {first_name},

{opener}

I'm Jack. I work as a solutions engineer in tech and live around Shepherd's Bush. On the side, my colleague Dayyan and I help local businesses get rid of repetitive admin with simple, personalised software and automations.

We build tools that run on your own computer, so you own them outright, with no monthly subscription.

The first chat and any discovery work are completely free. We'd come and hear what's eating your time and tell you what we could fix. You only pay if we actually build something.

Would you be up for a quick chat? Coffee, a phone call or Google Meet, whatever's easiest. Grab a time here: [Calendly link]

Jack

variants.label: TENET v2 variant A: late invoices and quotes
variants.text:
Hi {first_name},

{opener}

I'm Dayyan, a software engineer based in Shepherd's Bush. A friend and I help small trades firms stop invoices and quote follow-ups slipping: we build a small tool that runs on your own computer, and you keep it.

If nothing is worth fixing, I'll say so. No charge for a first look.

Could we do 15 minutes next week, by phone, coffee or video? Pick a time here: [booking link], or ring me on [phone number].

Dayyan

variants.label: TENET v2 variant B: enquiries that wait
variants.text:
Hi {first_name},

{opener}

I'm Dayyan, a software engineer based in Shepherd's Bush. I help small trades firms make sure a new enquiry gets a quick, sensible reply even when everyone is on a roof or under a sink, and the serious ones reach your phone first.

I'd like to hear how enquiries reach you now and whether anything is worth fixing. If not, I'll say so. First look is free.

Could we do 15 minutes next week? Pick a time here: [booking link], or ring me on [phone number].

Dayyan

variants.label: TENET v2 variant C: question first, for older owner-run firms
variants.text:
Hi {first_name},

{opener}

What's the one bit of paperwork you'd happily never do again? Invoices, certificates, chasing a quote?

I'm Dayyan, a software engineer based in Shepherd's Bush. I build small, fixed-price tools for trades firms that take that job off you, and you own them outright. A first look costs nothing, and if there's nothing worth fixing I'll tell you.

Could we do 15 minutes next week, either [Tuesday at 4pm] or [Thursday at 10am]? Phone or coffee, your pick. Reply with 1 or 2, or ring me on [phone number].

Dayyan

variants.label: v1 draft 1: credentials-led (use for about 80% of sends)
variants.text:
Hi {first_name},

I'm a software engineer, and I live about 10 minutes from {business}. My colleague Jack and I are helping a few local businesses get rid of the admin that eats their evenings: invoices that go out late, bookings typed in twice, the same email answered 20 times a week.

We don't sell software. We come in, look at how you actually work, and build a small fix that runs on your own computer. You own it; nothing to rent.

Could we buy you a coffee for 15 minutes next week and see if there's anything worth fixing? No charge for the first look.

Dayyan

variants.label: v1 draft 2: automation-led
variants.text:
Hi {first_name},

Jack and I are 2 engineers from round the corner. We build small automations for local businesses: invoice reminders that send themselves, website enquiries sorted and answered before you've seen them, stock or booking data moved between the tools you already use.

The difference from the usual: it runs on your own machine, you keep the code and the data, and we only use AI where a plain script can't cope. Most first fixes cost between £400 and £1,200, fixed price.

Free 45-minute session to map where your time goes, then a one-page list of what we'd fix and what it would cost. Worth 45 minutes?

Dayyan

variants.label: v1 draft 3: open problem-finding
variants.text:
Hi {first_name},

Odd question from a neighbour: what's the one job at {business} you'd happily never do again? The Sunday-night invoices, chasing a supplier, replying to the same booking question?

I'm a software engineer, Jack is too, and we're spending the next couple of months helping businesses within a 10-minute walk fix exactly that kind of thing with small, simple tools they own outright.

The first look is free: 45 minutes in your shop at a quiet hour, then a one-page note of what we'd fix and what it would cost. If nothing's worth fixing, we'll say so.

Dayyan

variants.label: v1 draft 4: trades angle
variants.text:
Hi {first_name},

I'm guessing you'd rather be on site than chasing invoices or reading through website enquiries to find the serious ones.

Jack and I are 2 engineers based locally. We build small tools for trades that send invoices and reminders automatically from the jobs you've finished, and sort incoming enquiries so the real ones reach your phone first. It runs on your own laptop; you own it, no monthly software fees.

Fixed price for a first fix, usually £400 to £1,200. A free 45-minute look first, at your yard or over a coffee, whichever suits.

Can I ring you one evening this week?

Dayyan

variants.label: Follow-up to v2 variant C
variants.text: Hi {first_name}, no pressure. Even a one-word reply naming the task you dislike most would help.
